text:
jordan: Quick sync — noticed a customer replay where our sidecar restart caused head-of-line blocking for a live gRPC streaming inference call. wondering if we should treat sidecar heartbeats and client cancel as separate control-plane frames so retries/early-accept don't conflate with connection restarts.

priya: Oof, saw that in traces yesterday. reproducer?

sam: repro steps: run a long streaming request (seq len ~4k tokens), kill sidecar, restart. client keeps TCP alive but server drops midstream. backend sees partial, gateway retries and we double-charge tokens.

kevin: can you paste the logs? sounds like our resume token path thinks this is idempotent and triggers a soft retry.

sam: log snippet:
```
EDGE: stream session 0x7f3c accepted (early-accept)
EDGE: sidecar heartbeat lost, reconnecting
EDGE: client CANCEL received (http2 RST_STREAM?)
GATEWAY: fallback -> retry variant model-small
BACKEND: request accepted 200 OK (billing +1)
```

priya: so problem is twofold: 1) early-accept + sidecar reconnect => we mark request as delivered, 2) client cancels but connection state ambiguous so gateway retries. we need stronger signal separation.

jordan: proposed: introduce explicit control frame `X-Edge-Control: heartbeat|cancel|resume` on the edge->gateway channel. sidecar restarts would emit `heartbeat` and not trigger any delivery semantics. `cancel` becomes authoritative — if we see cancel from client we don't spawn a retry unless server confirmed acceptance with an `ack` frame.

kevin: +1 on signal separation. slight concern: can't rely on clients to send that header. need to translate from HTTP/2 RST_STREAM / trailers into control frame at proxy boundary.

priya: agreed. translation layer in frontdoor: map `RST_STREAM` -> `X-Edge-Control: cancel`. For HTTP/1 chunked we'll treat `Connection: close` mid-body as cancel. For resume we already have resume tokens in metadata.

sam: also: billing attribution. if gateway forwarded to backend and backend returned 200 before we saw cancel, we should bill once. If we retried because we thought backend lost it, we double-billed. we need an idempotency marker per request that backend can echo (e.g., `X-Edge-Req-Id`) and our billing tallyer should dedupe on that id.

jordan: yep. minimal changes: 1) add control-frame translation layer at ingress, 2) add `X-Edge-Req-Id` header for all forwarded requests, 3) require backend echo for finality if we plan to retry. If no echo, treat as maybe-delivered and prefer fallback variants only for safe workloads.

kevin: sounds reasonable. one tradeoff: adding req-id echo requirement means some models/backends become ineligible for aggressive hedging. but we can gate that via model manifest (safe_for_retries).

priya: implementation notes: keep control frame handling in `edge-proxy/transport` so it works for both http1/http2/quic. add small state machine: ACCEPTED -> ACKED (backend echoed req-id) -> FINALIZED. Only create a retry path for states < ACCEPTED. That avoids retrying after backend ack.

sam: tests: failure-injection matrix: sidecar restart, network partition, backend slow flush, client RST. Also assert billing dedupe on req-id in local dev billing mock.

deploy-bot: rolling canary: edge-proxy/v2.19 -> 10% in us-west for 30m :rocket:

jordan: Action items: @kevin spike control-frame translator (this week), @priya add req-id echo in model manifest + billing dedupe, @sam write failure-injection tests. Will sync Friday for design sign-off. :thumbsup:
